local_only.description: If true, only allow local connections (no remote printer sharing). Set to false to share printers over the network.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait before considering a remote printer unreachable.

max_retries.description: Number of times to retry connecting to a failed remote printer before marking it unavailable.

retry_interval.description: Seconds to wait between retry attempts for unreachable printers.

items.description: Protocol(s) to use for discovering remote printers.

browse_remote_protocols.description: List of protocols for discovering remote CUPS printers. Common: 'cups', 'ipp', 'dnssd'.

items.description: Protocol(s) for discovering locally attached or networked printers via DNS-SD/CUPS.

browse_local_protocols.description: List of local discovery protocols. Use 'dnssd' for mDNS/Bonjour support.

create_remote_ppds.description: If true, automatically generate local PPD files for discovered remote printers. Disable only if managing PPDs manually.

default_options.description: List of default job options applied to all remote printers unless overridden.

name.description: Name of the remote printer queue to configure.

uri.description: Full URI of the remote printer (e.g., 'ipp://10.0.1.10/printers/HP-LaserJet').

make_and_model.description: PPD Make and Model string (e.g., 'HP, HP LaserJet Pro MFP M428f').

options.description: List of per-printer job options to apply.

printers.description: List of custom static printer configurations (override automatic discovery or predefine queues).

convertpcltops.description: If true, convert PCL to PostScript (for legacy PostScript-only printers). Usually unnecessary for modern IPP printers.

create_ipp_printer_queues.description: If true, create IPP-based queues (modern, standardized) instead of legacy CUPS queues. Recommended for network printers.

cups_local_server.description: Hostname or IP of the local CUPS server (the daemon communicates with this CUPS instance).

log_level.description: Verbosity of logging. Use 'debug' only for troubleshooting.

log_file.description: Optional absolute path to a dedicated log file. If empty, logs go to syslog.
